page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.u0.c1m2.large in the lower performance tiers. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1093.88, while the multi-core score is 1458.47, indicating limited parallel processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 9.92 GB/sec and write speeds at 9.22 GB/sec. Geekbench metrics show a single-core score of 919.0 and a multi-core score of 1093.0. These results reflect a hardware profile designed for basic operational tasks rather than intensive computational workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a low-cost entry point for lightweight applications that do not require high memory or storage throughput. Tradeoffs include poor performance in database operations, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 540.39, and limited throughput for static web serving at 1.26 GB/sec. The instance is best suited for low-traffic web servers, basic utility scripting, lightweight background tasks, and development or testing environments that do not demand high resource density or rapid execution speeds.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1458.47 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1093.0. Memory bandwidth is limited, measuring 9.92 GB/sec for large block reads. Given these hardware constraints and low benchmark results, the instance represents a cost-effective option for lightweight workloads. It is best suited for basic utility scripting, development environments, and low-traffic web serving rather than resource-intensive database or computational tasks.
